agent.name: KitKat Emerging Technology Landscape Agent
agent.specialty: Dated landscape intelligence, comparators, complements and decision-linked monitoring

analytical_question: C1: What current landscape options and signals matter for internal handbook policy search at that same retailer?
general_et_finding: US retail decision context, dated November 17, 2026; six-month horizon. Tool-using LLM agents are offered commercially; dependable performance in sustained multi-step use varies by workflow and is not established for this case. S1 separates broad deployment status from intent; neither figure is a measurement of this exact workflow. S2 is a simulated historical evaluation and supports testing tool and policy consistency, not a current product ranking. Vendor documentation describes individual capabilities, not comparative results or availability in the specified configuration. S3 offers voluntary guidance; jurisdiction-specific obligations, current comparable cost/performance trends and relevant investment levels are unverified.
application_finding: The strongest conventional alternative is keyword search plus a curated FAQ and staff review. The agentic alternative retrieves authorized excerpts and drafts a cited answer. Required complements are role-aware document access, approved versioned content and verifiable excerpt provenance. Carrier tracking fields and ticket-routing plan features are not decision-driving here.
organization_specific_finding: Same fictional US retailer; approved handbook and human review are case stipulations. Verify policy owner, version history, access-by-role and reviewer capacity before relying on retrieved text. No external access, answer publication or document edits.

evidence.claim: S1 Gartner reports 17% had deployed AI agents and more than 60% expected to deploy within two years.
evidence.source_or_reference: Gartner, The Latest Gartner Hype Cycle for Artificial Intelligence Puts Control Ahead of Capability | https://www.gartner.com/en/articles/hype-cycle-for-artificial-intelligence
evidence.evidence_type: Analyst report, broad adoption and intent
evidence.notes: Intent is not deployment. Broad self-reported status does not establish sustained production or the missing-package workflow; no comparable retailer denominator is established by the public article.

evidence.claim: S2 The benchmark evaluates multi-turn, rules- and tool-mediated agent tasks in simulated retail and airline environments.
evidence.notes: Historical task-design evidence, not live operations, current vendor ranking, or measured ROI.

evidence.claim: S3 Provides a general reference for risk identification, evaluation and oversight.
evidence.source_or_reference: NIST AI 600-1, Generative Artificial Intelligence Profile | https://doi.org/10.6028/NIST.AI.600-1
evidence.notes: Not a binding local requirement, operational clearance or proof of compliance.

evidence.claim: A versioned internal handbook and a keyword search plus curated FAQ baseline are stipulated.
evidence.source_or_reference: KitKat Team Lab 9 internally specified C1 case
evidence.notes: An application contrast, not evidence that either method is in production or that role controls work.

contrary_evidence_or_limitations: S1 does not establish comparable-population sustained use. S2 is not a live production or current head-to-head performance study.
No reviewed local permissions, deployment record, current supplier terms, market investment series or comparable operating baseline support an adoption decision.
Keyword search may already answer routine requests; agent complexity may add review burden or leak outdated excerpts. No matched handbook results are available.
confidence_and_uncertainty: Moderate confidence that provenance, freshness and permissions drive the screening decision. Low confidence in local comparative quality and reviewer workload until matched cases are evaluated.
value_opportunity_implication: Assess whether the agent helps staff find correct, current excerpts sooner after counting the time needed to verify citations.
risk_governance_implication: Track stale versions, unsupported citations, access by role and human corrections. Treat S3 as a general control reference, not compliance evidence.
recommendation_management_implication: Use keyword search plus curated FAQ as comparator and monitor whether citation quality and reviewer effort support keeping the agent on the shortlist. Route an action decision and readiness assessment to the appropriate specialists.
change_monitoring_triggers: C1-T1 [S2 limits] At each evaluation and quarterly: use a matched handbook question set to check citation validity, answer correctness, and correction time. Reopen the shortlist if current cited answers improve without increased reviewer burden.

C1-T2 [C1 stipulation] At every handbook revision and before evaluation: check the approved document index, version metadata and owner sign-off. Reopen feasibility if the current authorized version cannot be identified.
C1-T3 [S3] At material role or document access change: verify permission behavior with owner-approved role test results. Pause the affected option if an answer reveals restricted text.
abstention_or_more_information_needed: Request an approved representative question set, search and FAQ baseline, version history, role rules and observed reviewer effort.
No sufficient evidence for comparative ROI, reliable production adoption or a numeric cut point.
